PRACTICAL PROJECT / 2 OF 2
Queries and expected results

SELECT name FROM products
WHERE price > (SELECT AVG(price) FROM products);

SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders
GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;
Query 2 returns Kit (900 > average 500). Query 3 returns customer_id 1 with n = 2.

1. Add an order_items table with a composite key and foreign keys to products and orders.
2. Find all customers without orders using NOT EXISTS.
3. Add an index for customer_id and created_at and compare EXPLAIN.
4. Test a transaction by updating an order total and rolling back.
5. Explain where a unique payment reference belongs and why.

Scope based on Full-Stack SE Internship Checklist, page 7; Sections 04–34 Full-Stack Interview Study Guide,
pages 56–59. Further reference: MySQL 8.0 Reference Manual (dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/).
